topic: A parent finds an old letter they wrote but never sent
story: Roberto's breath caught in his throat when he recognized his own handwriting on the water-stained envelope. It was addressed to his son, Carlos, dated six months before Carlos had moved across the country for college. He ripped it open with trembling fingers. "I'm proud of you. I know I never say it, but..." Line after line of affection and encouragement, all things he'd never managed to say aloud. His vision blurred. Carlos was forty now. They'd maintained a polite but distant relationship for decades, and Roberto had always assumed it was because Carlos knew how his father felt, even if the words weren't spoken. His knees buckled and he sank onto the bed. This letter proved otherwise. He'd written it all down and then, what, chickened out?

topic: A parent finds an old letter they wrote but never sent
story: I found myself unable to move, staring at the letter in my hands like it was written in a foreign language. But it wasn't—it was my own words, addressed to James, my husband, dated three months into our marriage. "I'm not sure I can do this. I'm not sure I'm ready." My heart pounded against my ribs. We'd been married thirty-one years. I'd told him dozens of times about how certain I'd always been, how I'd never had doubts. This letter, forgotten in the back of my old filing cabinet, told a different story. My hands felt numb. Had I rewritten my own history? Convinced myself of a narrative that wasn't true? The paper crinkled as my grip tightened involuntarily.
